entries.meaning: Rama and Lakshmana approach Rishyamuka. The frightened Sugriva sends Hanuman, disguised as a young Brahmin student, to discover who these two mighty, tender-footed forest travellers are—perhaps the divine Nara and Narayana, or the Lord of all worlds incarnate to deliver creation and relieve Earth's burden.

Rama identifies himself and Lakshmana as Dasharatha's sons, exiled in obedience to their father and searching for Vaidehi, whom a demon abducted. Asked to tell his own story, Hanuman recognizes his Lord, falls at his feet speechless with joy, then admits that delusion and ignorance prevented recognition and asks why the omniscient Lord questioned him like an ordinary man.

Hanuman confesses his faults but pleads that a master must not forget his servant: a being entangled in the Lord's maya crosses it only by his grace. Claiming no means of worship beyond dependence, he reveals his true form and falls at Rama's feet. Rama embraces him tearfully, calls him twice as dear as Lakshmana, and defines exclusive devotion as the unwavering conviction: 'I am the servant; the Lord is manifest in all that moves and does not move.'

Reassured by Rama's favour, Hanuman proposes friendship with the exiled Sugriva, who can send millions of monkeys to seek Sita. He carries the brothers to Sugriva, who bows and marvels that providence has given him such friends. Hanuman relates each side's story; fire witnesses their solemn alliance.

The friends hold nothing back. After Lakshmana recounts Rama's story, Sugriva tearfully promises that Sita will be found and tells how he saw a captive woman crying 'Rama!' in the sky and throwing down a cloth. Rama presses it to his heart in grief; Sugriva promises every service, and Rama asks why he lives in the forest.

Sugriva recounts how the brothers Bali and Sugriva pursued the demon Mayavi into a cave. Ordered to wait a fortnight, Sugriva remained a month, saw blood flow, assumed Bali dead, sealed the cave and fled. Forced onto the vacant throne, he was later attacked by the returning Bali, robbed of kingdom and wife, and driven across the world. Rama's arms twitch at his servant's suffering, and he vows that one arrow will kill Bali even if Brahma and Rudra shelter him.
